additional: [untitled BTM module] Granulocyte development and activation is the theme here: a transcriptional core that commits myeloid progenitors to the neutrophil lineage, a cytokine receptor that drives their expansion, and signalling and cytoskeletal components that let mature cells respond. PU.1 and the retinoic acid receptor set and maintain myeloid identity, which is why blockade of retinoid signalling in promyelocytic leukaemia arrests cells short of maturity and why pharmacological retinoid treatment restores it.

shared: [untitled BTM module] This grouping describes a mesenchymal, fibroblast-like programme in which mechanical and growth-factor cues are converted into matrix remodelling and stromal activation. Its hallmark outputs, the secreted matricellular proteins CCN1 and CCN2, are canonical readouts of YAP/TAZ activity downstream of cell stretch, stiffness and Rho signalling, and caveolin-1 links plasma-membrane mechanics to that response.
positive regulation of focal adhesion assembly
additional: [untitled BTM module] These genes outline a mesenchymal, mechanoresponsive fibroblast programme in which YAP and its paralogue TAZ (WWTR1) convert cytoskeletal tension and matrix stiffness into transcription of matricellular and adhesion genes. CYR61 is a canonical YAP/TAZ target, and alongside collagen III, follistatin-like 1, caveolin-1 and VCAM1 it marks cells that build and remodel connective tissue and support leukocyte and progenitor traffic.

[untitled BTM module] These genes mark the resident fibroblast and perivascular stromal compartment of connective tissue, the cell population that builds and remodels extracellular matrix and supplies growth signals to neighbouring epithelium, endothelium and immune cells. Matrix and matrix-associated products such as tenascin C, ECM2, OLFML3 and the BMP antagonist chordin-like 1 shape tissue architecture and the diffusion of morphogens, while locally produced complement components C1S and C7 give stroma a role in innate immune surveillance.

additional: [untitled BTM module] Granulocyte maturation in the bone marrow, and the antimicrobial cargo that neutrophils acquire as they mature, is the theme here. Promyelocytes and myelocytes load their granules with proteins that will later be deployed against bacteria: a lipopolysaccharide-binding bactericidal protein of the BPI family, the adipokine-like secreted factor resistin, prokineticin 2, the soluble pattern-recognition molecule pentraxin 3, and a haematopoietic growth factor of the CLEC11A type that supports progenitor expansion.

[untitled BTM module] These genes mark the antimicrobial granule programme of neutrophils, the arsenal that granulocytes build during maturation in bone marrow and deploy against bacteria and fungi at sites of infection. BPI binds and permeabilises Gram-negative outer membranes through its affinity for lipopolysaccharide, lipocalin 2 sequesters bacterial siderophores to starve microbes of iron, and olfactomedin 4 defines a distinct subset of neutrophil specific granules; CEACAM8 is a surface glycoprotein used routinely to identify granulocytes and their precursors.

[untitled BTM module] The dominant theme here is transmembrane solute handling in polarized epithelia of liver and kidney, coupled to regulated vesicular secretion.
